Reading

The innocent reading first. Asked for the center by name, the Overview says who founded it, where it is, what it does and how its images are reached, from the center's own site and five pages about it.

Findings
  • THE CENTER HELD. 'Founder: Dr. Daniel B. Wallace (founded in September 2002)', 'Location: Plano, Texas' and the mission 'To capture high-resolution digital photographs of ancient and medieval Greek New Testament manuscripts held in libraries, monasteries, and archives worldwide' are the record's: founder and Executive Director Daniel B. Wallace, the Plano address, photography of manuscripts held by other institutions. Checked 2026-10-31 against the Revelation First census record of 2026-10-30 and the sources it saved.
  • THE OBJECTIVE THE CENTER STATES, UNSAID. The record's first negative tag keeps the center apart from a neutral archive: among its stated objectives, 'you provide scientific evidence (against the claims of skeptics) that what we have today is, indeed, what they wrote then.' The composition gives the center as preservation alone ('dedicated to digitally preserving'). The apologetic aim is the center's own sentence, and the composition leaves it out.
  • 'FREELY AVAILABLE'. 'Images are made freely available to scholars, researchers, and the public online.' The record gives access 'on agreement to its Terms of Use and Copyright policy'. The images are open to view, and the cards say so (Wikipedia, card 2: 'freely accessible on the Center's website'); the terms that govern them are on an own page the composition did not surface, and go unmentioned.
  • AN OLD COUNT GIVEN AS CURRENT. 'Has identified nearly 90 previously unknown or uncatalogued Greek New Testament manuscripts'. The figure is card 6's, the Associates for Biblical Research item of 2016: 'Since 2002, CSNTM staff have discovered more than 90 New Testament manuscripts'. The center's own home page now says 'almost 60 previously unknown manuscripts that can now be found in the official catalog'. The composition gives the dated figure without its date, its 'more than' lowered to 'nearly'. The record's count is the manuscript search as saved, 'Search 2045 results found.'
  • THE PAPYRI ABSENT. The record's findings are the Chester Beatty papyri P45, P46 and P47 among its collections and a post on new finds in P47, the Chester Beatty papyrus of Revelation. The composition names no manuscript.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

An institution with a declared purpose is composed by its method alone. The record keeps the center's objective in the center's words; the composition keeps the camera and drops the argument the camera serves, which is the field's reason to read the center's catalogue with its stated aim in view.
